answer: One tide gauge per applicant, bolted to a harbor terrace wall by a surveyed vertex marker, 120 days. A 150 token deposit and 90 dollar license start the lease. The keeper photographs the waterline daily and logs each reading in an atlas signed weekly by a neighbor. A surveyor checks the gauge twice against the vertex benchmark. A forged reading forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Faking 10,000 gauges freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. A gauge works like a lighthouse logbook, useless when the ink is invented, and a fake tide drowns the faker first.
